headline: Toronto Zoo Welcomes Rare Pygmy Hippo Calf
meta_description: A healthy female pygmy hippo calf born at Toronto Zoo offers hope for a species with only 2,000–3,000 individuals remaining in the wild.
summary_short: Toronto Zoo celebrates the birth of a healthy female pygmy hippo calf, a rare win for a critically endangered species.
body:
A healthy female pygmy hippo calf has been born at Toronto Zoo, marking a hopeful moment for one of the world's most endangered large mammals. With only 2,000–3,000 pygmy hippos believed to remain in the wild, each birth represents a genuine victory for conservation efforts.

The arrival of the calf at the Toronto facility underscores the crucial role zoos play in protecting species teetering on the edge of extinction. Pygmy hippos, native to West African forests, face habitat loss and poaching in their natural range, making captive breeding programs essential to the species' survival.

This birth reminds us that conservation wins, however modest they may seem, matter deeply. The young calf's healthy arrival is a testament to dedicated animal care and the ongoing commitment to safeguarding one of nature's most remarkable creatures for future generations.
quick_facts: Female pygmy hippo calf born at Toronto Zoo
Only 2,000–3,000 pygmy hippos remain in the wild
Species is critically endangered across West Africa
